harbor_p07_001.speaker: narrator
harbor_p07_001.text: The commercial hearing room had no place for a tub, which disappointed Wen Zhi. He wanted the object present so nobody could pretend its value existed only on paper. The clerk placed the maker's drawing and inventory images of marks on the table instead, identifying their sources. T4 remained in secure upstream custody. Yue sat at the permitted observer bench with her inquiry board. Miao arrived carrying both leaves of the release packet in a plain folder, as though keeping them together now could answer for the week when they separated.

harbor_p07_002.speaker: narrator
harbor_p07_002.text: The reviewer was an ordinary harbor official named Song An, licensed to decide commercial claims within the posted charter. Sui Yan supplied technical records but did not decide title. Qin Shuo supplied wage bond references where needed to prevent accounts being confused. The reviewer read the listed questions aloud and asked each party whether a relevant source had been omitted. Wen named his customer's messages. Miao named the employer's purchase invoice. Both were included, and both would have the chance to explain them. The clerk marked each request before the first comparison began.

harbor_p07_003.speaker: narrator
harbor_p07_003.text: Wen's loan agreement identified six tubs by maker's marks and required return after one voyage, subject to safe handling. The merchant's invoice described purchased contents packed in those containers. A later letter accepted the maker's identities while reserving the cleaning question. No supported later sale of the tubs was produced. Song compared the terms in front of the parties. Fresh blue paint showed use, not transfer of ownership. Wen gripped his drawing so hard its lower edge wrinkled while the reviewer asked Miao for any remaining source. The agent slowly shook his head.

harbor_p07_004.speaker: narrator
harbor_p07_004.text: Miao still believed the merchant could retain the containers until the contents sold, because returning them made storage difficult. Song asked which term allowed that. The invoice did not. The loan agreement allowed safe clearance time, not indefinite commercial convenience. Miao looked toward Qian Du, whose expression remained blank. The reviewer recorded the distinction and moved to contents rights. Losing the container claim did not mean the merchant had never owned what the tubs carried. The agent looked relieved to have at least one supported part of his employer's account survive.

harbor_p07_005.speaker: narrator
harbor_p07_005.text: The purchase and inventory records established the merchant's rights in cleared contents, including R4, within technical handling conditions. Spoiled material could not be sold as though clearance covered it. The merchant could choose lawful disposal or a permitted review, but restricted residue would not become Wen's burden simply because it rested inside his containers. Sui Yan explained the handling estimates through their sources. Song asked whether the representative disputed a particular estimate. Qian requested the breakdown rather than rejecting the total alone. The captain moved the three pages closer to him.

harbor_p07_006.speaker: narrator
harbor_p07_006.text: The licensed handler's estimate separated twelve copper for cleaning six containers from ten for safe disposal of spoiled contents. The loan agreement required clean return. The goods account covered spoiled material. Qian confirmed authority to agree for the merchant and accepted the supported twenty-two-copper charge subject to actual completion and receipts. The money would come from the merchant's cargo operations account. It would not reduce a worker's paid wage or come from the two-hundred-fourteen guarantee remainder. Wen looked pleased until he saw that cosmetic paint restoration was not part of cleaning.

harbor_p07_007.speaker: narrator
harbor_p07_007.text: Wen wanted fresh paint removal added. The handler said safe cleaning covered residue, not the original appearance. Song asked whether the loan terms required the old surface restored. They required sound, clean containers, with damage beyond normal use separately assessed. Paint had been applied over maker's marks without removing them. Wen could submit a supported damage question, but no immediate extra sum followed from disliking blue. He stared at the inventory image and muttered that sound tubs ought to look sound too. Miao almost smiled, then thought better of doing it there.

harbor_p07_008.speaker: narrator
harbor_p07_008.text: The reviewer examined T4's departure. The R4 order required a clean receiving container and retained the separate hold. Miao's carrying note said take as packed. The messenger delivered two leaves to the store. The storeman separated conditions into cleaning estimates. Lu received the shortened copy and carrying note, although he earlier acknowledged the tub remained held. The gate attendant failed to check its tag against full conditions. Song read each act beside its source. Nobody could hide inside the passive phrase the tub was moved. The chain had names and recorded decisions.

harbor_p07_009.speaker: harbor_qin_shuo
harbor_p07_009.text: The guarantee deposit has its own conditions. It covered supported unpaid wages, which have been paid. It did not authorize these cargo instructions. I brought the ledger because public comments proposed using the remainder for recovery costs. That would make a convenient purse from money held for another purpose. The question today is who bears documented costs under commercial and port rules. If a party owes them, that obligation needs its own source. My balance cannot supply it. The fact that I still hold copper does not let us ignore why it came here.

harbor_p07_010.speaker: narrator
harbor_p07_010.text: Song asked Miao whether he knew T4 remained held when he signed. The agent said yes. He expected the yard to wait for a clean receiving container, despite the dispatch phrase. The reviewer noted the conflict between expectation and instruction. Habit did not make the words harmless. The bonus term explained an interest in reducing loss, but evidence did not establish he intended to steal Wen's container. Song distinguished an unsupported title demand, careless direction, and alleged concealment. Each would receive its own finding. Miao stared at the folded pages while the clerk wrote.

harbor_p07_011.speaker: narrator
harbor_p07_011.text: The storeman admitted separating the condition leaf. Its heading resembled technical estimates he regularly filed elsewhere. The yard supervisor had assigned him route preparation, including complete transfer conditions. Song asked whether that duty appeared in the roster. It did. The explanation supported a classification mistake but did not remove duty. The recovered leaf and preparation register allowed the reviewer to say what happened without inventing a secret instruction from Miao. Qian stopped suggesting the messenger dropped it. The storeman sat straighter after hearing that particular suspicion leave the supported account.

harbor_p07_012.speaker: narrator
harbor_p07_012.text: Lu said a signed merchant note should have been enough for a hired porter. Song asked why he sought no confirmation after the explicit T4 warning. Lu said it would have cost another unpaid wait. The reviewer accepted the pay arrangement as context and recorded his decision to proceed without resolving the conflict. An expensive wait did not become a lawful exception. Lu watched the page as though its lines were walls. He had expected the employer's signature to carry more burden. The clerk gave him time to read the recorded answer.

harbor_p07_013.speaker: narrator
harbor_p07_013.text: The gate supervisor supplied the two-post staffing record and acknowledged insufficient cover for conflicting releases during busy intervals. The attendant was still required to check held tags. Song identified the missed check and staffing responsibility. Sui sat silent while the supervisor spoke. The failure concerned commercial release, not her sample findings, but its result required her staff to intervene. The harbor contained enough responsibility for several offices to feel weight without turning it into undifferentiated blame. Yue noticed how quickly people became attentive when a general failure acquired a task they had actually accepted.

harbor_p07_014.speaker: narrator
harbor_p07_014.text: Cost claims produced a quieter argument. Gao Lin's pilot record supported seven copper in extra crew and berth charges. Wen documented four for the tracing cart and three for secure storage. Replacement-container hire cost four. Customer cancellation linked a price dispute and delay, so full expected profit was not accepted as proven loss from the move. Wen had supplied both messages and understood why. Supported immediate costs totaled eighteen, not every number anger first imagined. He asked the clerk to preserve the rejected question with reasons, so he could consider review without rewriting his evidence.

harbor_p07_015.speaker: narrator
harbor_p07_015.text: Song allocated the supported eighteen under the charter after hearing the parties: twelve from the merchant's cargo account for conflicting instructions and route preparation; three from Lu through an agreed civil settlement; three from the port's authorized release-services correction allocation for condition-check and staffing failures. Each had notice and a review route. The administrator approved its three before payment. Lu agreed from his own purse, without invented wage withholding. Qian signed within supplied authority. The clerk read the sources aloud so the total could not look like money appearing merely because an official wanted fairness.

harbor_p07_016.speaker: narrator
harbor_p07_016.text: The hearing ended before disposition papers were ready. Wen was furious he could not collect tubs that afternoon. Song pointed to accepted cleaning and completion checks. The title direction would require return after those conditions, with a date and route. Miao looked exhausted. He lost the broad tub claim and acquired an account of instructions he actually gave. Yue left permitted notes with Han Pei for filing and went outside. Warm air made the room's damp wool unpleasant. A gull cried over the board as though announcing something more decisive than anyone inside had managed.

harbor_p07_017.speaker: narrator
harbor_p07_017.text: He Ming waited by the tea stall with cooled dumplings. She asked whether the reviewer called Miao a thief. Yue described supported findings: the conflicting direction, separate duties, documented costs and allocations; deliberate theft was not established. He Ming sighed, then asked whether Wen would get the tubs. The title direction required return after safe cleaning. She ate a dumpling and said that was what she wanted before learning to want punishment too. Yue took one beside her. The filling tasted better than the cold wrapper deserved, which gave them another subject.

harbor_p07_018.speaker: narrator
harbor_p07_018.text: Wen joined them carrying his wrinkled drawing. The rejected profit claim annoyed him though he understood its reason. He had pictured the canceled job buying replacement timber for his workshop. He Ming asked whether timber could wait. Some could, he said; one cracked shelf could not. Yue offered no fund. He had other stock and an ordinary business choice. He looked toward the harbor, then said he would repair the dangerous shelf first and dislike the remaining week afterward. He Ming laughed, recognizing a reasonable plan that did not require its maker to feel cheerful.

harbor_p07_019.speaker: narrator
harbor_p07_019.text: Miao ate alone until Han Pei sat opposite with plain rice. She would not discuss protected employment details in the public stall. He wanted no advice, he said. She had offered none. They ate in silence until it became less hostile. He asked whether the office would call his note careless forever. The record kept the act and consequence, she said; people might also see what he did next. That frightened and relieved him. Han finished her bowl before he decided whether to answer. Their shared meal had not given him a private appeal.

harbor_p07_020.speaker: narrator
harbor_p07_020.text: Qian left the next morning after arranging merchant payments and telling Miao to finish cargo work. He took no bond remainder; its review belonged to Qin's separate process. His departure removed one pressure and left the agent with ordinary unfinished tasks. Miao brought complete packets fastened through both leaves to the release desk. The clerk checked them without praising redemption. A method mattered when it survived becoming routine. Yue saw the new bundle on the counter and thought the clerk's quiet acceptance gave Miao a more useful future than a speech about changed character would.

harbor_p07_021.speaker: narrator
harbor_p07_021.text: The written title decision identified Wen's containers, supported contents rights, twenty-two copper in cleaning and disposal, and eighteen in transfer costs. It gave dates, completion evidence, custody references and review. The public notice omitted irrelevant private employment terms. Parties received reasons within access rights. Yue copied status for worker-property outreach so nobody would mistake it for wages reopening. The harbor's papers said more than pending dispute now. People still had to carry the results out. The decision's edge curled in the damp, and Han placed a weight on it before answering the next visitor.

harbor_p07_022.speaker: narrator
harbor_p07_022.text: Handlers cleaned four tubs at the main berth and two through the upstream arrangement, recording containers and disposal batches. The merchant paid twenty-two after completion receipts matched estimates and tasks. Wen inspected soundness and cleanliness with the clerk present. One loose hoop required comparison with arrival condition. The handler secured it before transfer within the agreed task. Wen did not get a perfect new tub. He got his own in a supported usable condition. He pressed the hoop, asked the handler one more question, and finally said it would do, sounding surprised by his own acceptance.

harbor_p07_023.speaker: narrator
harbor_p07_023.text: T4 returned on an ordinary shore cart after stage custody closed and the commercial desk acknowledged receipt. No crew performed a celebratory lift. The tub traveled secured like any approved load with a driver who knew its route. Wen counted six and signed collection. Yue saw his shoulders lower for the first time in weeks. The drawing returned to his coat. Its wrinkled edge had become part of the ordeal. He would press it under a board at home, he said, though the mark would probably remain. Yue thought that sounded like several things returned by the harbor.

harbor_p07_024.speaker: narrator
harbor_p07_024.text: The eighteen-copper costs were paid: seven for pilot charges, four for tracing cart, three for secure storage, four for replacement hire, each under receipts. The merchant supplied twelve, Lu three, the approved port allocation three. Shared responsibility did not reimburse any expense twice. Canceled expected profit remained outside the accepted total with reasons and review. Wen's full disclosure made the account stronger where it reduced his claim. He read the receipt carefully and asked for one spelling corrected. Even at completion, a name deserved the trouble of an accurate line.

harbor_p07_025.speaker: narrator
harbor_p07_025.text: After settlement, Lu asked whether waiting time could appear in carrier contracts. The clerk directed him to the labor advice desk. He looked disappointed, then took the reference. Miao agreed to specify paid dispatch waits for remaining work. The new term did not erase T4's move. It changed one pressure that encouraged him to proceed. Yue heard this through the completion account and wondered how often prevention began as an unglamorous sentence about an hour. Lu returned to a cart with ordinary ropes, looking neither defeated nor transformed, merely more aware of a question he could ask.

harbor_p07_026.speaker: narrator
harbor_p07_026.text: Han and Yue's next inquiry shift focused on the destination packet. The supervisor's reply, exchanged-cart tally, yard instruction and slips supported a mistaken outward transfer. No source established Miao directed the packet aboard. Permit accounting remained separate. Han wrote the supported conclusion and the gap about who folded the destination inward. Yue checked quotations instead of improving them into a satisfying plot. The real account had consequences enough. Its ordinary sequence showed how useful information could be mishandled without a master conspirator, and still leave duties worth examining and people owed correction.

harbor_p07_027.speaker: narrator
harbor_p07_027.text: He Ming read the conclusion and felt foolish for imagining merchant concealment. Han said the benefit justified asking, not concluding. The woman asked whether public summaries should distinguish allegations and findings before people made a story. The clerk agreed to propose clearer lines. Their conversation no longer required Yue between them. She listened at the copying table while two women who hurt each other found questions neither could write alone at the beginning. He Ming offered an example. Han challenged one word. The disagreement sounded almost companionable, though each still wanted the other to understand.

harbor_p07_028.speaker: narrator
harbor_p07_028.text: Peng returned the plane with its edge sharpened. The apprentice approved the edge and disliked the wrap's ship smell. Peng bought clean cloth himself. He recovered his adze and admitted the loan without losing his trade. At the boat yard, he won the repair job He Ming suggested and complained that the borrowed replacement was too sharp. The story reached supper in three versions, each funnier. Yue had heard only one firsthand and enjoyed all three. Ordinary humor was allowed to improve a tale when no claimant's money depended on which version somebody believed.

harbor_p07_029.speaker: narrator
harbor_p07_029.text: Fen helped copy a public notice using the contents-and-container drawing. Her paid shift followed the full conditions reference instead of squeezing everything onto a scrap. Luo watched after sorting work and admitted he would read the drawing first. Both mattered, she said. He asked whether the kite needed one. Its sea claim remained ridiculous, she replied. He said the sea had not answered in time. Fen laughed at a legal joke she understood now for reasons he regretted. Their ordinary work had supplied a shared language neither would have chosen through weeks of fear.

harbor_p07_030.speaker: narrator
harbor_p07_030.text: Fen brought the joke to the shed. The boy insisted silence meant the fish won. Han said a missing reply granted no such claim. He accused the office of favoring gulls. Yue laughed until the kite bumped her head. In the dry square, mild wind held it above roofs. Ordinary air lifted it without qi. Fen kept the spool while the boy ran beneath an imaginary court whose defendant never agreed to attend. Han's gull painting appeared on the other side, and the two creatures shared the sky much more easily than their advocates shared the argument.

harbor_p07_031.speaker: narrator
harbor_p07_031.text: Qin began the remainder review on the ninth week's middle morning. The schedule showed six hundred forty-two earned, ninety-six paid earlier, five hundred forty-six paid from seven hundred sixty, leaving two hundred fourteen. Notices and the challenge window had run. Recipient disputes resolved before collection. Unknown property bundles did not create wage claims automatically. The merchant requested return under the guarantee rule. Qin checked no properly supported hold remained. His trainee read the receipt references alongside him. The custodian looked less troubled by sharing the task than he had when opening the deposit weeks before.

harbor_p07_032.speaker: narrator
harbor_p07_032.text: A former worker asked the review about a private meal loan. He supplied crew food and thought the bond should cover it because their wages passed through the voyage. Qin explained covered obligations and directed the contract question to the civil desk, which received it under its own reference. Proximity did not make the debt wages. The man disliked the answer but had a route instead of being told the harbor finished all business. Yue watched him read the new receipt. The closed wage account still lived in a town where people could owe one another other things.

harbor_p07_033.speaker: narrator
harbor_p07_033.text: Wen wanted the two hundred fourteen held until the tubs survived another job. Qin asked whether the guarantee covered container quality. It did not. The title decision and supported damage review remained available commercially. Returning the deposit erased no such obligations. Wen stared at the wage ledger, then said he understood and wished money were easier to follow. Yue shared that wish. Purpose became most visible when an account refused to become the purse everyone thought would solve an immediate problem. Wen took the commercial reference and kept it beside the drawing in his coat.

harbor_p07_034.speaker: harbor_qin_shuo
harbor_p07_034.text: There is no virtue in keeping money because it feels safer than returning it. We received the deposit under a rule, used it for supported claims, and answer the return request under the same conditions. If another account owes repair, injury support or restitution, its duty survives without borrowing this balance. Workers received what they earned. The merchant has the supported remainder. Neither cancels mistakes we still review. We keep the record without keeping money it no longer permits us to hold. I would rather explain a sound return than let an unjustified hold pretend to be care.

harbor_p07_035.speaker: narrator
harbor_p07_035.text: The written decision authorized two hundred fourteen returned after ledger and notice checks. The designated recipient supplied the depositor's authority. Miao did not collect merely because he handled the voyage. Qin counted copper with the keeper and recorded transfer. The account closed at zero after five hundred forty-six wage payments and two hundred fourteen returned. Yue liked closed arithmetic and disliked how little closure it gave people around it. An account could end before consequences did. The keeper put the empty deposit box back onto its shelf, ready for another properly identified purpose someday.

harbor_p07_036.speaker: narrator
harbor_p07_036.text: Miao watched the recipient leave. His twenty-copper bonus required an untouched deposit, so proper wage draws meant no bonus. His fixed agency fee belonged to the separate employment term. Han asked whether he needed advice on any unpaid fee. He expected payment and would ask if it failed, he said. He sounded less eager to make every difficulty proof someone else should lose a claim. The change was small enough to believe. He fastened a new dispatch packet with both leaves attached and asked the clerk to check it before the carrier left.

harbor_p07_037.speaker: narrator
harbor_p07_037.text: Qin took a free afternoon in shore gardens where a retired sailor grew onions among boat fittings. Yue met him buying seedlings for the shed keeper. He used to sail a little, he said, before preferring to know where his chair stood at dusk. Did ledgers give certainty? He laughed. They supplied a chair and a long list of ways to worry while sitting. The gardener offered them eggs from an ordinary basket and told Qin his seedlings would die if he continued watering them like accounts requiring daily attention. The custodian accepted the rebuke.

harbor_p07_038.speaker: narrator
harbor_p07_038.text: They ate on a sun-warmed wall. Qin's hands trembled more often now, and he was training a second keeper in tasks he once refused to share. He feared she would think him unnecessary. Yue asked what happened when only he knew a procedure. Everybody waited if he was ill. That had flattered him and now frightened him. The morning handover belonged to his work. He needed no public lesson made from it. The gardener called him over to inspect a broken hinge, and Qin went happily to a problem whose answer could be held in one hand.

harbor_p07_039.speaker: narrator
harbor_p07_039.text: The handover used the closed deposit ledger and a blank practice account. The trainee checked arithmetic, authority, custody and receipts while Qin watched. She caught an intentionally incomplete return instruction and sought its missing source. He looked pleased, then embarrassed by his pleasure. Han witnessed through funded ordinary staff time. Yue observed the portion her appointment permitted. A functioning process could outlive particular hands she first saw open the book. Qin could take another garden afternoon. His trainee asked one difficult question about late claims, and he admitted he wanted to read the rule again before answering.

harbor_p07_040.speaker: narrator
harbor_p07_040.text: Sui received the maritime inspector's report. The partition and access structures required repair before any new voyage. The master could arrange approved work at the repair berth after hold disposition. Cargo quarantine closed only its technical conditions; it did not certify seaworthiness. He was angry, though less theatrical. His ship had actual tasks to price instead of an argument about harbor hatred. Yue watched him reading the list against the rail. He rubbed his forehead, then called his carpenter. Anger could remain while the work became specific enough to begin, and that seemed an ordinary useful outcome.

harbor_p07_041.speaker: narrator
harbor_p07_041.text: Yan visited the repair berth about temporary mooring and work boundaries. The ship carpenter disliked an outsider naming rot he inherited. Yan said his platform review taught him how inheritance became an excuse for a check never made. The carpenter listened without thanks. They inspected accessible faces and identified controlled opening tasks. Yue later read their authorized report rather than claiming to witness every conversation. Competent work happened beyond her paid half-days. At supper, Yan mentioned the carpenter's clever brace proposal with respect, proving that an uncomfortable first exchange did not require a lifelong enemy to follow it.

harbor_p07_042.speaker: narrator
harbor_p07_042.text: He Ming settled the remaining room account for her mother's visit. The landlord showed dates and charges; the bedding deposit returned after inspection. Her own room seemed larger without complaints about the window. She bought a plant from Qin's garden friend and put it where Mother kept a cup. Yue said the plant might criticize light. He Ming preferred a tenant drinking less tea. She checked the soil, then admitted she missed the cup. The plant could occupy the space without replacing the person. Its leaves were ordinary green, almost absurdly peaceful above a table crowded for weeks with receipts.

harbor_p07_043.speaker: narrator
harbor_p07_043.text: He Jun returned with a delivered family letter and a story about missing the creek connection by three minutes. He paid his extra inn night himself. He Ming inspected the letter and asked whether he learned to leave earlier. Yes, until next time, he said. She laughed instead of lecturing. They agreed the next collection point before his new packing job. His life could move while contact remained something actually done. He offered to cook supper, then discovered her mother took the seasoning jar home. The family had managed another departure with a minor act of theft everyone could forgive.

harbor_p07_044.speaker: narrator
harbor_p07_044.text: Luo's care review allowed broader finger movement and still barred heavy gripping. He called the splints expensive decorations. Fen preferred decorations with instructions. The binder offered a month of paper sorting at a clear rate and schedule. Luo accepted. Recovery and earnings could share a calendar. His voyage wage helped him refuse another unsafe loading shift in desperation. That practical freedom was absent from the public sum. At home, he tried the prescribed exercise while Fen practiced characters. They criticized each other's posture until both threatened to leave the room, then stayed because the lamp was there.

harbor_p07_045.speaker: narrator
harbor_p07_045.text: Fen asked the tea seller for fewer washing evenings to take copying shifts. A transition date followed hiring ordinary help. She did not vanish because another job pleased her. She taught the new worker where customers hid chipped cups and which table leg needed a folded wedge. Luo watched his daughter leave a task manageable by someone else. He never thought that leaving could be a skill. The tea seller paid the final agreed shift and told Fen she remained welcome as a customer. The girl looked proud and slightly bereaved while putting her work cloth away.

harbor_p07_046.speaker: narrator
harbor_p07_046.text: Dai brought a net to He Ming and asked whether she would sell it on commission. He Ming offered an introduction, declining to keep another person's account. Dai understood. She wanted work rather than permanent gratitude toward someone who helped return a comb. They negotiated directly with the shore seller. Yue later saw them laughing at a wrong knot in a customer's sample. Grief remained while the trade had its difficult useful days. Dai charged for repairing the knot instead of treating it as a favor. The seller accepted, and the women walked home discussing prices for ordinary thread.

harbor_p07_047.speaker: narrator
harbor_p07_047.text: The protected-address claimant acknowledged payment through her chosen route. Han shared the relevant completion status without private words. He Ming asked no name. Would future contact processes preserve the same choice? Existing rules did, Han said; practice needed to make it understandable. Their proposed help chair should not pressure family contact as the price of wages. He Ming agreed, then asked whether someone refusing all help still received a clear calculation. Han showed the plain receipt form. The desk could offer assistance without making dependence another condition of being believed. Yue added the example to their proposal notes.

harbor_p07_048.speaker: narrator
harbor_p07_048.text: The administrator wanted evidence of outreach time beyond ordinary desk duties. Yue supplied completed shifts and results, including unsuccessful leads. Han supplied staff notes without blaming every delay on a missing employee. He Ming described wrong walks. Yan described work-line reporting. None promised limitless coverage. Costs, dates and responsibility were needed before continued work. Care could begin discussion but not appropriate money. The administrator asked which task mattered most in the next month. They answered differently. Yue found the disagreement useful because the proposed term would have to choose rather than pretend one visitor could perform every necessary job.

harbor_p07_049.speaker: narrator
harbor_p07_049.text: The old yard owner arrived for next week's permit review. Zeng Kai had a polished stick and persistent cough. He asked why the address method became his problem when workers supplied inconsistent information. Han produced signed summary approval and retained individual slips. He admitted approving a shortened list, denied directing false lodging status. The distinction mattered; actual fees and instructions decided more than irritation. He asked to see the full comparison, which the review clerk arranged within access rights. Yue watched him read his signature for a long time, as though a familiar mark could look different after months away.

harbor_p07_050.speaker: narrator
harbor_p07_050.text: Zeng called He Ming troublesome about packing deductions. She said they were wrong. The permit clerk sought a relevant source if either relied on that history. He had none about this address decision. Her yard history did not decide the current account. Yue admired the effort required to prevent a contest over respectability. Zeng's stick tapped until he realized everyone heard it. He stopped. He Ming supplied the actual former-room account she consented to use, keeping private family letters covered. The clerk examined the relevant date and asked a question that allowed her anger to become precise evidence.

harbor_p07_051.speaker: narrator
harbor_p07_051.text: Zeng asked whether Yue belonged to a court or powerful household. She described the inquiry appointment and end date. The ordinary answer disappointed him. Visible fourth-stage arms granted no permit authority. He could answer the named desk and sources. Yue felt temptation to let vague reputation stand where something useful belonged. She named the clerk again and resumed comparison. The owner spoke more sharply after learning she was not a secret envoy. It made the room less pleasant and more accurate. He would have to confront the actual review rather than negotiate with a power imagined behind her face.

harbor_p07_052.speaker: narrator
harbor_p07_052.text: The former yard clerk would answer by witnessed letter because travel exceeded his current employer's permitted absence. The office arranged source access and response through its review duties. Zeng disliked remote testimony. The clerk explained how documents and questions would be tested without gathering everyone. The owner requested written questions and received them. Yue thought of the lower court routes she once helped make possible. The harbor needed its own practical version, not a borrowed ceremony. A reply arriving by ordinary messenger could still be examined, corrected and weighed, provided its source and limits came with it.

harbor_p07_053.speaker: narrator
harbor_p07_053.text: Han's late packet preparation used approved ordinary overtime. Yue's inquiry shift ended before the cabinet reopened. She brought requested supper and charged its actual private cost. Han ate while checking public headings, telling Yue to stop looking solemn. She knew the pay and would leave after two packets. Friendship need not call every long desk evening exploitation. It needed the bargain heard. Yue apologized for hovering and sat with her own tea. Han finished one packet, made a small mistake in the other, corrected it, and then kept the promised end rather than making exhaustion a virtue.

harbor_p07_054.speaker: narrator
harbor_p07_054.text: Walking home, Han asked whether painting would waste clerking years. Yue said those years existed in what she knew; next work needed choice and support. Han wanted both, which sounded childish aloud. Two modest schedules might fit where an imagined transformation did not. Duan's yard was shuttered. Han would ask about a paid beginner session after review, she said, instead of resigning in a midnight mood. Yue admired the decision's lack of drama. A person could alter a life through a timetable small enough to keep, and discover whether desire survived having actual hours attached to it.

harbor_p07_055.speaker: narrator
harbor_p07_055.text: On her rest morning, Yue practiced with a light thread marker. The steady interval matched established fourth-stage control. She stopped before fatigue and noted duration rather than inventing progress from calmer thoughts. Harbor patience and questions did not automatically become another realm. She mended a sleeve after putting notes away. The wrapped pendant remained beneath her spare shirt, absent from cargo and rescue accounts. Downstairs, the boy lost a spoon and blamed the gulls. Yue helped look beneath the table with ordinary hands. They found it beside a shoe, which seemed a more probable culprit than anything in the sky.

harbor_p07_056.speaker: narrator
harbor_p07_056.text: The boy asked to copy Han's gull onto the kite. She consented to a personal drawing and warned paint added weight. He proposed a tiny gull riding the fish. Yue thought travel looked inconvenient for both. Fen said most travel was. They held paper flat while he ignored their commentary. Patchwork recorded evenings together, outside an official inventory. The tail still needed repairing after its last flight. Luo offered a thread from an old cuff with permission. The kite took the contribution and carried a little piece of the recovered chest into an entirely different sort of journey.

harbor_p07_057.speaker: narrator
harbor_p07_057.text: Wen invited He Ming to see his repaired shelf. Yue came on a free afternoon with consent. Peng, paid for brace work, complained Wen inspected screws like a hearing. Wen said they held valuable stock. They bickered comfortably. Yue touched the brace and liked a story ending in a shelf holding its intended things. The workshop smelled of shavings and oil. Six recovered tubs stood under cover. Their blue paint annoyed Wen less now that he had other work to argue about. He asked Peng whether the next brace could be cheaper, and Peng told him to ask the screws.

harbor_p07_058.speaker: narrator
harbor_p07_058.text: Wen showed an older maker's mark cut by his brother. He kept the drawing because memory became unreliable after death. His brother died years earlier from fever; tools passed through ordinary family division. Wen chose containers over boats because they stayed in one place. T4's ordeal offended that reason as well as his account. He Ming listened gently. The private story did not enlarge accepted damages or change title. It made the man at the angry window easier to understand. Yue saw how many people's practical choices were built around grief no public notice ever had reason to explain.

harbor_p07_059.speaker: narrator
harbor_p07_059.text: Miao sent completed cost accounts without an apology. Wen disliked the omission and admitted he would distrust fine words. The agent's next packets separated contents and containers with all conditions attached. An ordinary check found no mismatch. One correct packet proved a useful next act rather than permanent character change. Yue saw it pass to a carrier who read both leaves. The action lacked grandeur. It helped a cart depart without another hold violation, which was enough work for that morning. Tomorrow would ask for the method again, and success would begin looking ordinary if they kept doing it.

harbor_p07_060.speaker: narrator
harbor_p07_060.text: Sui received notice the platform review needed another comparison before final findings. Immediate care support continued properly. Deren's lost-work claim had a named date. The captain gave her roster and resumed completion work; Yan supplied inspection routines. Their friends could want a fair account without insisting it favor them. Yue found that hope more demanding than imagined loyalty. Deren stopped by the quay to complain about delay, then asked Yan to help him carry a stock list indoors. They did it together. Neither acted as though the pending question had erased everything useful between them.

harbor_p07_061.speaker: narrator
harbor_p07_061.text: The ninth week's last shift completed eighteen initial half-days, earning thirty-six of forty-eight wage copper. Expenses remained six each for copying, interpretation and ferries within separate twenty-four ceilings. Cargo title directions and costs were recorded. The deposit closed after returning two hundred fourteen. The full wage total remained paid. Permit review and durable-contact proposals were remaining work. Yue refused to make closed accounts look unfinished because the town still had questions. Han checked the shift record beside her. It showed limits as well as results, and left three actual weeks rather than a vague promise of further help.

harbor_p07_062.speaker: narrator
harbor_p07_062.text: Han carried her painted board home so no visitor mistook it for a seal. Yue joined her through the market, where early peas were offered loudly. They split a small bag and ate some raw before remembering supper. Han called it poor resource accounting. Yue said the loss had identifiable recipients. Laughter followed them beyond the stalls. A woman washing her step told them to keep clear of fresh water. They moved obediently and kept laughing. Ordinary limits could be obeyed without turning every encounter into a test of who held authority in a town.

harbor_p07_063.speaker: narrator
harbor_p07_063.text: He Ming waited at the shed with Mother's letter. She arrived safely and found the creek room dusty. He Jun returned as promised. Mother intended no imminent death simply because everyone now asked whether she reached places. He Ming read that sentence three times. Yue laughed until the boy asked why. Love sometimes sounded like a complaint from someone pleased to have an audience, the woman said. She tucked the letter among her own papers, keeping its public delivery receipt separate. The room still felt quiet, though now its quiet had a voice she could reread.

harbor_p07_064.speaker: narrator
harbor_p07_064.text: The permit hearing notice went up the next morning with Zeng's name and the former clerk's reply route. It concerned lodging-status entries, charged fees, approval duties and correction. Paid wages would not reopen because old addresses appeared there. Workers could give accounts without surrendering private family letters. Yue had three initial-term weeks left. The sea beyond the landing shone. The harbor measured itself against work it might owe after a visitor departed. She looked at the date, checked the appointment in her own calendar, and went to buy breakfast before the next queue began forming.
